en: Preface to the Newly Carved Record of Xuansha I humbly submit that when the Buddha expounded the Three Vehicles, it was like a lamp transmitting its light through the nightless darkness. When the School divided into five branches, it was truly so that the Dharma continued the intent of non-arising.
In former times, the Venerable Xuansha Bei was renowned throughout the four seas and was revered by all practitioners of Chan. His realization was transcendent...

He cut off the path of conceptual discernment; with no-mind, he was the very mind itself. His model for the Way left behind a lingering fragrance, and his profound principles overflowed throughout the world.

Having been in the East for several years, I was able to read the published edition of the *Extensive Record of Xuansha* (Xuansha Guanglu) with the preface by Sun Jue from the Yuanfeng era of the Song dynasty.
Alas, as the ages have passed in China, it had long been submerged and lost to hearing. Fortunately, thanks to the land of Fusang, there were those who preserved this treasure. How could this be...?

Is it not the case that the Great Dharma is manifest everywhere? Now, having encountered the newly carved edition being circulated by Chan Master Rongfeng of Anguo Mountain, may all people see and hear it, together planting the supreme conditions for *prajñā* and restoring the ancestral style of a thousand ages.
An unerring and enduring grand monument has been established; herein, only its general outline is recounted. I hope that those of like mind will examine it.
This brief preface is written by Donggao Yue and Dudo together. *Preface to the Extensive Record of Xuansha*.
Written by Sun Jue of Gaoyou, Right Reminder and Director of the Jixian Academy, serving as Military Governor of Fuzhou and Commander of the Military Forces of the Fujian Circuit.

The study of Buddhism encompasses the greatest variety of paths, yet Chan is particularly prone to many ailments. During the height of the Tang dynasty, the Northern and Southern schools alternately disparaged one another.
In the north, Chan gradually declined. What can be seen today consists of more than a thousand houses, all of which originated from the Sixth Patriarch.
In recent times, discourse on Chan has flourished even further; however, only the Yunmen and Linji lineages have been transmitted.
From the scholars and gentlemen of the imperial court down to the commoners bustling in the streets and alleys, there are none who do not vie with one another in their mastery of Chan.
I have studied them with great devotion and diligent inquiry, and have likewise grasped their general outlines.
Thus, regarding the subtle words and discursive arguments of ancient and modern Chan practitioners that have appeared between the lines of brush and ink, I have searched for them almost exhaustively.

Master Xuansha’s *Beishi* was renowned throughout the four seas and held as a patriarchal authority by Chan practitioners; yet, while I have guarded this [text] for nearly two years, I could not obtain its complete edition. It was only late that I finally acquired it.
Volumes five and six were incomplete and fragmentary; Master Sengjiao collated them and combined them into a single book. Although not entirely complete, ten volumes have now reached seven or eight.
Consequently, he commissioned the monk Xuansha to carve woodblocks so that they might circulate in the world.
According to this, Master Zongyi Shibei was a native of Min County, Fuzhou, whose secular surname was Xie. At the beginning of the Xiantong era, he followed Master Yixuan of Furuoshan.
The Master Tong served Great Master Hongzhao for a long time. Later, he went to Kaiyuan Temple in Zhongling to receive full ordination from Vinaya Master Daoxuan.
Great Master Xuefeng once remarked, "Bei the Dhūta is a man who has returned for a second birth. Bei replied, "How can I travel to various regions?
The First Patriarch did not come to this eastern land, and the Second Patriarch did not go to the Western Heaven. He remained at his original residence.
At the beginning of the Guanghua era, Wang Shenzhi invited Xuansha to be the founding abbot of Anguo Temple. Those who followed him as students numbered over seven hundred.

Huiqiu and Guichen were both his most eminent disciples. Wang Shenzhi submitted a memorial to the throne requesting that he be granted the purple *kāṣāya* and the title "Zongyi" (The One of the Lineage).
He passed away in the eleventh month of the second year of the Kaiping era at the age of seventy-four. (From the *Yuanfeng San*)
Preface on the twenty-seventh day of the intercalary month of the year.
Compiled by the junior disciple Zhìyán, who studied under the Great Master Xuánshā Zōngyì of Fúzhōu,
from the Extensive Record [of the Master], during the third year of the Guānghuá era, the cyclical year Gēngshēn.
The Master ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying: "Do you all truly comprehend the ocean of wisdom of the *prajñā* of the fundamentally pure nature and characteristics?
If you have not yet comprehended it, then consider this: as you are gathered here together, do you see the green mountains before you?
If you say you see them, how do you see them? If you say you do not see them, what then of the green mountains?"

"I say: 'I do not see. Do you understand? All you venerable elders, it is simply that within your own pure, fundamental nature, the ocean of prajñā-wisdom of both essence and characteristics is fully present for seeing and hearing. If you understand, it is just so;
if you do not understand, it is also just so. I have stood long; take care."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Every phenomenon is eternally thus; every nature is like this. One must strictly avoid seeking it externally.
If you possess the great faculty of faith, know that all Buddhas are nothing other than the self-enjoyment samādhi of each person. Walking, standing, sitting, or reclining—it has never not been so.
I am now speaking directly to you: to do so already degrades the noble to the lowly. Will you accept such a statement? Or will you not?"
Furthermore, how do you understand this? To speak as I am doing now is already a failure to recognize good from evil.
Why is this so? It is because you people make such distinctions as "this" and "that. [The Master] stood for a long time. "Take care! Question:
"What is the samādhi of self-enjoyment? The Master said: "Why use so many samādhis? The questioner asked further: "How is it then?"
"It is so. The Master said, "How could it not be so? He ascended the hall and said:
"These mountains and waters penetrate through the three periods of time. With their constant murmuring, there is nowhere they are not present.
You venerable monks, the mountains are mountains; the waters are waters; the three periods are the three periods. How can you say they 'penetrate' one another? Therefore—"
"I have explained to you that throughout the worlds of the ten directions, there is nothing that is not this very place. You must attain it in this way before you can succeed.
Even further supernatural powers and transformations would be of no avail against you. You must personally realize the nature of your own self before you can succeed.
Do not linger; each of you must exert yourselves. Take care."
The Master said to the assembly, "The Buddhas constantly assist all of you; do you understand? If you understand, where do you understand it?
If you do not understand, how is it that you do not understand? Furthermore, do you all accept this, or do you reject it?"
Question: “What is the place where all Buddhas assist those who study? The Master said: “You assist me. Question:
“Who is the person who directly refuses to accept [the teaching]? The Master said: “Which one is your elder brother Ming who refuses you?
[The student] further asked: “Why is it so? The Master said: “A thousand miles, ten thousand miles.”
Ascending the hall, he said: "What are you all seeking here by undergoing such hardship and suffering? It is not that I am unwilling to open my two flaps of skin [to speak].
Why is this? The gateway of the mouth has no efficacy; it is not words and phrases that can bring peace to a person.
You must proceed with total oneness (*yīrú*) before you will attain resonance. Do not merely recite words and phrases—what end will there ever be to that?"
It is simply a single, seamless whole. Do not say that one must reach the level of the various sages’ functioning before one can attain freedom.
Where are you all not equal to them? Question: "When one has attained such oneness, what then? The Master said:
"Why do you speak in your sleep?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "I have resided here for eight or nine years. Throughout the twelve hours of the day, there has not been a single moment of change.
It is brilliantly clear. But how do you understand this? Do you see it? Master Shanzhong said: 'Everyone possesses a mirror of antiquity.
From the beginningless past to the endless future, what kind of thing is it that I am pointing to when I speak of it?'"
"It is then called the 'ancient mirror. Do not merely say it is as usual; you must take it as a matter of actual practice. Do not treat it with indifference. A question was asked:
"How should one apply the mind throughout the twelve periods of the day? The Master said: "To ask such a thing is quite perverse. The student pressed further: "..."
"Will you attain it or not? The Master said, "It is still like talking in one's sleep.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The great earth and empty space are all the wondrously luminous true mind. Do you all understand?
Have you not seen how Master Shanhe constantly said to people whenever he met them, 'What is this? You monks must truly..."
Only when you have attained self-conviction will you succeed. Do not merely spend your time in groups of three or five, prattling on about this and that.

While you may find a sense of peace for a while, it will be difficult to obtain a human body again in the future. You must be diligent day and night; only by drawing near to spiritual companions and engaging in decisive discernment will you finally achieve success.
The Master, upon meeting a newly arrived monk, asked, "Venerable sir, where have you recently departed from? The monk replied, "I have departed from Xuefeng.
The Master asked, "What words has Xuefeng recently used to instruct people? The monk said, "Recently the Master told the monks, 'Here it is like an ancient mirror:
when a barbarian comes, a barbarian appears; when a Han person comes, a Han person appears. At that time...
A monk asked, "What if a bright mirror suddenly comes upon you? Feng said, "Both barbarian and Han are hidden. The Master said, "I do not speak in that way.
That monk then asked, "Venerable Yanxiang, I inquire of the Master: what if a bright mirror suddenly comes upon you?
The Master said, "Shattered into a hundred pieces! He added, "Brother Xiang, how does the Master of Mount Shan compare to me in this regard?"
"The Way. To speak of it thus—do you understand yet? The student asked, "Yanxiang does not understand; what is your Reverence’s intention?
The Master said, "As for you, Brother Xiang, how can you say you do not understand? The Master then said, "O virtuous ones, Master Zhongshan said:
'I am here like an ancient mirror. When a barbarian comes, a barbarian appears; when a Han person comes, a Han person appears.'"
Manifest! I shall now speak directly to you: this is a single-sided bright mirror. But how do you understand it?
It is just like when my brother asked me, "If one suddenly encounters a bright mirror, what then? I told him, "A hundred pieces, a thousand fragments.
Now, how do you all understand this? If you can understand it, it is simply your own fundamental matter of inquiry, vast and profound.
“I have stood here for a long time. Take care.
Because Xuefeng was traveling to the capital, the Master went out to meet him. He said, “The journey must have been difficult; I am glad you have arrived. Xuefeng said, “Indeed, indeed.
The Master said, “Nyo! Nyo! (A sound of acknowledgment. Xuefeng said, “If it were not for you, it would also have been difficult. The Master said, “It is as it is.”
"This is merely because it was my home village; it was not due to my own ability. Feng said, "I know you have attained it.
You must speak to others about it. The Master said, "Yes, yes. He is just like this. Feng asked, "Do you know how the one named Lingdao questioned Lingyun?
The Master said, "I do not know what he asked. Feng said, "Lingdao asked: 'What is the Buddha-dharma?'"
The general meaning is as follows. Daoyi said, "The matter of the donkey has not yet gone; the matter of the horse has arrived. Master [Xuefeng] asked, "Does the Way-farer Ling understand?
Feng said, "He does not understand. The Master said, "Why do you not tell him so? Feng said, "I told him: 'Right here is you.
The Master said, "If it were like that, I fear his karmic conditions would no longer lie with you, Master. He then instructed [him].
Later, when Xiyi arrived, I said to him, "When Fenyang departed, he said, 'You are the abbot here; you must take full responsibility for this place.
The Master said, "I have received it, O Monk. Fenyang said, "Clouds naturally arise and depart. The Master said, "When the Abbot reached the mountain..."

"You must also take good care of yourself. Feng replied, "Yes, yes. Feng returned to Mount Shan and said to Daozhe Leng, "When I went to Xuan Sha's place, I brought up the karmic conditions regarding your question to Lingyun.
Xuan Sha understood it very well. Leng asked, "I do not know what Xuan Sha said. Feng replied, "He simply said, 'You are Daozhe Leng. Leng said, "..."
"Master, why do you not explain this to me? Feng said, "Was it not just now that I explained it to you?
Leng said, "If that is so, I shall go for a moment to pay my respects at Xuansha's place. Feng said, "If that is so, then go there for now."
The Master said directly to him, "I do not understand. Go on your way; may you return soon. Lingren then descended to the master’s quarters. The Master said, "I am glad you have come down.
I heard you asked about the Great Meaning of the Buddha-dharma regarding Lingyun—is that so? Lingren replied, "It is. The Master asked, "What did he say to you?
Lingren replied, "He said, 'The donkey's business has not yet gone, and the horse's business has already arrived. The Master said, "Do you understand?"
Molu said, "I have no understanding at all; I have come specifically for this reason. I beg the Master’s compassion to explain it for me.
The Master said, "You are the practitioner Leng; why do you not understand? Molu said, "I do not know what the meaning was in Lingyun speaking thus.
The Master said, "It is simply you, practitioner Leng; do not seek it externally. Molu said, "What about the Master?"
Sheng spoke thus: "I cannot fail to know my own name; I beg the Master to explain its meaning for me.
The Master said, "You are a man from Liangzhe, and I am a man from Fuzhou. Why do you not understand? Leng said, "I truly do not understand;
I beg the Master to explain it to me. The Master said, "How could I be failing to tell you? Leng said, "I have come here specifically..."
Dizang came forward and requested, "Venerable Master, please explain this for me; do not deceive me like this. The Master asked, "Do you hear the sound of the drum?
Lingmo replied, "I cannot claim not to recognize the sound of the drum. The Master said, "If you hear the sound of the drum, it is simply you. Lingmo said, "..."
"No. The Master said, "Go and eat your congee first. After the practitioner Leng had finished eating, he went up to the hall and said, "I beg the Master to explain it clearly.
The Master said, "It is not that you have finished eating congee. Leng said, "I beg the Master to explain it clearly; do not play games with me."
The monk was about to take his leave and depart. The Master asked, "By which road did you come? Ling replied, "I came by the Da-mu road.
The Master said, "When you go, you shall also go by the Da-mu road. How can you say you are deceiving me? Go in peace."
A monk came from Xuefeng. The Master asked, "What sayings has the Abbot of the Mountain been using to instruct people lately?
The monk said, "The Abbot of the Mountain says, 'On the southern mountain there is a tortoise-nosed snake;
you all must watch it carefully. The Master asked, "Is there anyone who understands this? The monk said, "An Upādhyāya named Ling from Zhejiang replied, 'Today...'"
"In this hall, there are many who lose their bodies and forfeit their lives. The Master said, "One must be a man like the Wayfarer Ling to achieve this;
I do not speak in such a manner. A monk then asked, "How would you speak, Reverend? The Master said, "What need is there for the Southern Mountain?
[The monk] asked, "What is the tortoise-nosed snake? The Master said, "I am telling you; what need is there for the Southern Mountain? The monk—
Question: Xuefeng said, "On South Mountain there is a single turtle-nosed snake. What is the meaning of this? The Master said:
"It is right here before you; it is you who do not understand. The monk said: "I do not understand. The Master said: "Neither do I understand."
One day, while a monk was paying his respects, the Master said, "Do you all recognize the boundaries of this place—the east, west, south, and north?
Xingsi replied, "I recognize them all. The Master said, "The Buddha-dharma is not a matter of such principles. A monk asked: [the Master continued: "..."
"What are the boundaries to the east and west? The Master said, "Old man Xie, you yourself just now said you did not know.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The Buddha-dharma is a matter of no-thought; it can both give life and take life. To see one's nature and become a Buddha is a principle that penetrates past and present.
A monk asked, "Since this is the Buddha-dharma, why is it able to take life? The Master said, "You are alive."
A man stepped forward and asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma of the living? The Master said, "You are a dead man. The Master went up to Xuefeng to pay his respects.
After the formal greetings, Xuefeng said, "Go down there and see how those others are doing. The Master went to the Hall Master’s quarters;
as soon as he entered the door, he lifted his sitting cloth (zuoju) and asked the Hall Master, "What is this mind? The Hall Master replied, "What kind of mind is this?"
He went on. The Master said, "The Buddha-dharma is not this kind of principle. He then went to the bathhouse and saw the Venerable Fu of Taiyuan twisting a water-towel.
The Master said, "Venerable, let us have a look at one another. Fu said, "We have already looked at each other. The Master asked, "In what year? Fu then returned to his room.
Later, when the Master went up to Xiangfeng, he said, "I have thoroughly exposed the Venerable Fu. Xiangfeng [said], "..."
Yun asked, "How will you examine him? The Master then recounted the previous conversation. Yun said, "His words are indeed there.
The Master said, "This old fellow has not yet even touched the ground with his heels."
While Xuefeng and the Master were walking on a mountain, Xuefeng said, "I wish to turn this stretch of ground into a field of merit.
The Master said, "Look at this ground; it would be well-suited for building a seamless stūpa. Xuefeng then made a gesture of measuring the land.
The Master said, "It is indeed so, yet I do not see it that way. Xuefeng asked, "How do you see it? The Master said, "Building a stūpa. Xuefeng said, "Excellent! Excellent!"
The Master said, "Attained, Reverend.
The Imperial Protector Wang of Quanzhou had invited the Wayfarer Ling to reside at Zhaoqing. Xuefeng dispatched a messenger with a letter to the Master’s location.
The Master asked, "From where have you come? The monk replied, "From Xuefeng. The Master said, "The Buddha-dharma is not this."
Regarding this principle: When the Master was seeing off the practitioner Leng at Xuefeng, they looked at one another and he said, "Preceptor, you may rejoice;
another branch has now spread from there. Xuefeng said, "Yes, yes. The conditions are indeed such, but it simply does not reach my native place.
The Master said, "He is certainly settled. Xuefeng said, "Yes, yes. The Master said, "Nyo! Nyo! [Later], the Master saw the practitioner Leng.
[The Master] came to see him and said, "You are a person of merit; the Grand Chancellor has built this monastery for you.
Lingmo said, "This kindness is entirely due to the Abbot and the Venerable Master; it is not from me. The Master said, "I have come up here specifically for your sake.
How do you intend to repay me? Lingmo said, "If that is so, I shall prostrate in thanks to the Master. The Master said, "No."
Regarding this principle, the Master then related the anecdote concerning Xuefeng’s question to the practitioner Lengdao.
Xuefeng said, "He was originally a man from the Two Zhe regions. Lengdao replied, "Quanzhou is certainly not his native mountain. The Master said, "If that is so..."
"Go there and maintain the monastery well," the Master said. Ling replied, "Yes, yes. The Master said, "I originally did not have the surname Xie.
Ling said, "And when was I ever a native of Suzhou? The Master said, "It is so, it is so. It must be like this before it can be achieved.

Ling said, "Everyone has their own ancestral roots; one must be clear about this before it can be achieved. The Master said, "One must also apply it where it is appropriate; it cannot be taken as a mere unity."
Xiangling said, "Everything depends on the occasion. The Master said, "Excellent, excellent! Very good indeed. Xiangling said, "Yes, yes. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Do you all yet recognize the matter of traveling on pilgrimage? I shall now tell you directly:
the Buddhas of the ten directions and I have studied together; we have traveled together as companions in the Way, day and night, never for a moment apart."
Is this so? Do you understand? If you understand, understand it right now. If you do not understand, how can you say you do not understand?
Do not merely go on weaving such verbal entanglements. Take care.
One day, the Master picked up a radish and asked a monk, "What do you make of this radish?
Over a hundred people, both before and after him, offered responses, but none were in accord with the truth. Later, Yuanchang replied, "I am eating it, Master.
The Master said, "What are you eating? Yuanchang said, "I am eating the radish. The Master said, "You know it! You know it! The Master then continued, "As for me..."
I have come to ask you all about this thing that is eaten. It is because you do not understand it that you merely seek out intellectual repartee;
what end will there ever be to this? I shall now speak directly to you: "To receive the words, one must understand the source. "Eaten" refers to the act of eating itself.
Use this; do not fail to distinguish between black and white. I tell you this from time to time: you must discern the pure from the defiled.
Do not be so muddled; such a state is impossible. Throughout the twelve hours of each day, I have never failed to take this as my primary concern, yet even so, it remains thus.
Do not say that a single turning word will suffice; that too is merely the ordinary.
"If it is so, let everyone fly high and soar far at their own will; there is no need to stumble here.
A monk then brought out a radish, turned back toward the mountain, and asked, "What about this, Master? The Master said, "I only want you to eat it.
The monk asked, "What is the radish that is eaten? The Master said, "When you are full, I am full."
Ascending the hall, he said: "O worthy ones! One dharma does not constitute one dharma; different dharmas do not constitute different dharmas. Do you understand?
If you do not understand, that too is non-understanding. If you do understand, that too is non-understanding.
Worthy ones, where is there for you to find awakening? If you awaken, it is just as it is; if you do not awaken, it is just as it is. Upādhyāya!"
What kind of principle is this, that it is so difficult to comprehend? Seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing are ever-present.
O worthy ones, regarding such discourse, what words are these? It must be clearly understood that all people must first attain oneness.
A monk asked, "What is the one dharma? The Master said, "The distinct dharma. The monk pressed further, "What is the distinct dharma? The Master said, "Oneness."
Fahui asked, "What is the Buddha-mind? The Master said, "The mind of sentient beings. He pressed further, "What is the mind of sentient beings?
The Master said, "The Buddha-mind. He asked, "What is the student’s own self? The Master said, "Why would you use your own self?"
Question: "What is it like when practitioners meet? The Master said: "When did I ever know you? Question:
"Who is the true host at Xuansha? The Master said: "You are the host; I am the guest. The student pressed: "Why is it so? The Master said: "What are you asking?"
Xuefeng asked the Master, "While you were staying there, what brothers or close associates did you have? The Master said, "All are those in training;
all are those beyond training. Xuefeng said, "I do not speak in that way. The Master said, "It is so. It is so. I do not speak in that way either. Xuefeng asked, "How then?
The Master said, "Not learning is complete learning. [The Master] was asked: "When seeing form, one sees the mind. What is this 'seeing'?"
[The student] said, "Form. The Master said, "The seeing mind. [The student] asked, "What is the seeing mind? The Master said, "Seeing form.
[The student] asked, "Are form and mind distinct or not? The Master said, "They are both distinct and not distinct. [The student] asked, "How do they accord when one realizes them?
The Master said, "They accord precisely when one does not realize them. [The student] asked, "What is the eye of the student? The Master said, "What is your name? [The student] approached.
[The Master] said, "It is bright and clear. The Master asked, "Do you yet recognize this eye?
He ascended the hall and said, "From antiquity to the present, there has truly not been a single dharma that is not so. Do you all know this?"
I now ask you: Do you see the mountain stream? Do you see the Buddha hall? Do you see the monks' quarters?
If you say you see them, by what means do you see them? If you say you do not see them, yet right now this mountain stream is clearly sounding with its gurgling flow.
The Buddha Hall and the Sangha Hall are right here before you. How can you say you do not see them? You venerable seniors, the mountain stream is the mountain stream;
the Buddha Hall is the Buddha Hall; the Sangha Hall is the Sangha Hall. But how will you understand this?
Question: "What is the Buddha Hall? The Master said: "I do not even recognize the Buddha Hall. Question: "What is the Sangha Hall? The Master said: "It is not the Sangha."
The Hall Master asked, "What is the mountain stream? The Master said, "It is not the Minqing River. The student pressed further, "How does one realize it?
The Master said, "There is no need to realize it. The student asked, "What is the matter of the separate transmission outside the teachings of the Three Vehicles? The Master said:

"How is it that this is not the matter of a separate transmission outside the teachings of the Three Vehicles? [The student] asked: "I beg the Master to assist me regarding the place where words do not reach.
The Master said: "This dead man! [The student] asked: "What is 'this Dharma abides in its own position'? The Master said: "You have fallen into such a state of inversion. [The student] asked:
"What is the state of affairs before all Buddhas appeared in the world? The Master said: "Of what use is it to you?"
"What are you doing? [The student] replied, "Is it not this very thing? The Master said, "This deluded fellow. He then ascended the hall and said:
"Since the Buddhas appeared in the world, they have manifested compassion and exercised pity; yet these are like flowers in the sky—lacking any solidity or substance.
You people must know that there is one who has never appeared in the world, nor has ever entered extinction. It is a phantom transformation, a phantom name; it does not exist."
"There is reality. Why is this? Because the nature of these four great elements is fundamentally empty and still; they have never ceased, nor have they ever arisen.
Furthermore, they have never taught and transformed sentient beings. The nature of sentient beings is as it is, and the physical body is likewise as it is.
Because the nature of sentient beings ceases, the physical body also ceases. Do you understand this yet? If you do understand it, come forth and let us debate it together."
If you do not know how to attain it, I shall now speak directly to you: the self-nature is unborn as self-nature; the self-nature is unceasing as self-nature.
How, then, can you comprehend this? O worthy ones, do not merely say that this nature is originally such.
If you understand, then I invite you to look at this before the assembled multitude. If you do not understand, then in what respect are you not equal to those Buddhas?
You must simply be thus before it can be attained. Those of superior capacity understand it all upon hearing it once; those of middling capacity also understand it upon hearing it once;
and those of inferior capacity likewise understand it upon hearing it once. To speak in such a theoretical manner—what kind of talk is this? Do you know? Do you?
Do you understand? It is fully present in every person; it is manifest in every person. A question was asked: "What is the manifestation of the Buddhas' compassion?
The Master said: "Cats and dogs. The questioner pressed: "Why is it so? The Master said: "What are you asking?"
Question: "What is the nature of the four great elements as being fundamentally empty?
The Master said: "Why do you undergo so much hardship? Question: "What is the self-nature that is unborn? The Master said: "By whom have you attained it? [The student] further asked:
"If that is so, then all dharmas are non-arising. The Master said: "You are merely deluded and inverted. Question: "What is the wondrously luminous reality?"
Xin. The Master said, "Venerable Jian, I see you asking such a question. [The student] asked, "What is it like when light and darkness have not yet been distinguished?

The Master said, "Black as ink. [The student] further asked, "What is it like after they have been distinguished? The Master said, "Black as lacquer. [The student] said, "I beg the Master to speak directly.
The Master said, "Was what I just said not direct?"
Lingyun arrived. After they had looked at one another, the Master asked, "How is it there compared to here? Lingyun said, "It is simply the mulberry and paulownia trees;
there is nothing else. The Master said, "Is it present or not? Lingyun said, "Constantly so, constantly so.
The Master said, "Why do you not say something? Lingyun said, "What is there to say? The Master said, "If it is truly so, then please speak. Lingyun said, "Three."

For ten years I have sought the swordsman; how many times have the leaves fallen and how many times have the branches sprouted? Since the moment I first beheld the peach blossoms, until now I have had no further doubts.
The Master said, "How great is your ability to cultivate your native roots! Yunyun replied, "I say this because it is not an external thing.
